_comment: Copy to config.json and edit. config.json is gitignored. Fundamentals below are ILLUSTRATIVE SAMPLE VALUES so the engine runs offline without live data — they are not current and are not investment advice. `fcf`, `shape`, and `narrative` power the decision + timing lenses of the dashboard. `narrative` is a CANNED sample standing in for the LLM 'agent voice' — the deterministic engine makes every call; the narrative only reads it back.

skill._note: Global valuation assumptions + a neutral mega-cap watchlist.

watchlist.name: Apple Inc.
watchlist.narrative: Agents read a fortress balance sheet, but at 15y payback the price already banks a decade of flawless execution — nothing on sale here.

watchlist.name: Microsoft Corp.
watchlist.narrative: Cloud and Copilot keep cash flow compounding, yet the multiple leaves no margin of safety — a great business at a full price.

watchlist.name: NVIDIA Corp.
watchlist.narrative: Agents flag accelerating datacenter demand; the discount to sticker reads as the market pricing a cyclical pause, not a broken thesis.

watchlist.name: Amazon.com Inc.
watchlist.narrative: Retail margin recovery plus cloud reacceleration give the cash story room, and price sits just under fair value with a short payback.

watchlist.name: Alphabet Inc.
watchlist.narrative: Search cash flow is intact and payback is reasonable, but price sits a hair above sticker — one good pullback from a buy.

watchlist.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
watchlist.narrative: Earnings power is real and payback is short, yet the rich price versus a conservative sticker keeps this on the bench.

watchlist.name: Exxon Mobil Corp.
watchlist.narrative: Cash returns are healthy, but low modeled growth pushes sticker far below price — the cushion just is not there today.

watchlist.name: Johnson & Johnson
watchlist.narrative: Defensive cash flow and a decent payback, but slow growth leaves the price above a prudent fair value estimate.

watchlist.name: Walmart Inc.
watchlist.narrative: Steady defensive compounder, but a 14y payback says the market is paying up for that stability — not cheap enough.
